title: Conduct treatment processes for wood destroying organisms

lessons.title: Subterranean termite treatments
lessons.html:
Preparing for the treatment

Before treating, confirm the identification (subterranean termites, not drywood termites or beetles), the extent of activity and the treatment plan. Use only a termiticide registered for the situation, at the label rate. Locate water pipes, electrical cables, drains, boreholes, wells and ponds; obtain building plans if available. Inform occupants and remove pets and food from areas to be drilled.

Pre-construction soil treatment

  1. Coordinate with the builder so treatment is done after the foundation trenches and fill are prepared and before the slab is cast or the damp-proof membrane is laid, as the label requires.
  2. Apply the calculated volume evenly over the area under the slab and along foundations, using a coarse spray.
  3. Do not treat when the soil is waterlogged or rain is imminent, as the label directs.
  4. Issue a treatment certificate stating product, rate, area and date.

Post-construction treatment

  • Trenching and rodding: dig a trench along external foundations to the depth the label specifies, treat the soil as it is replaced, and rod treatment into soil where trenching is not possible.
  • Drilling through slabs: drill at intervals along internal walls, cracks, expansion joints and around pipes, then inject the termiticide under the slab. Plug and seal the holes neatly.
  • Baiting systems: install in-ground stations around the structure, monitor them and add bait when termites are present, according to the system instructions. Baiting avoids large volumes of soil treatment and suits sensitive sites.

Safety and environmental care

Wear PPE as the label requires, including eye protection and a dust mask or respirator when drilling. Check for services before drilling; contact with electrical cables can be fatal and damage to pipes can spread termiticide. Never treat near wells, boreholes or ponds unless the label permits it and protective measures are taken, and never allow termiticide to enter drains or heating ducts.

lessons.title: Wood borer and drywood termite treatments
lessons.html:
Treating timber in situ

Most wood borer infestations in roofs, floors and furniture are treated with a registered timber insecticide applied directly to the timber.

Roof space treatment procedure

  1. Assess access and safety: stand only on structural members or boards, beware of fragile ceilings, check wiring and isolate power where damaged, and plan for heat by working early in the day.
  2. Clean timber surfaces of dust and cobwebs with a brush or vacuum so the product can penetrate.
  3. Cover water tanks, insulation and stored items where the label requires.
  4. Apply the product as a coarse spray or by brush to all accessible surfaces of the affected and adjacent timber, at the label rate, paying attention to joints and end grain.
  5. Inject product into exit holes or drilled holes where deeper penetration is needed.
  6. Ventilate the roof space and keep occupants out for the period the label specifies.

Furniture and joinery

Treat unpolished surfaces such as backs and undersides, or inject into exit holes. Test on a small area first because some products can mark finishes. Advise the client to keep the item in a ventilated area during drying.

Replacement

Where timber is structurally weakened, recommend removal and replacement with treated timber by a competent builder.

Drywood termites and severe infestations

Drywood termites and severe or concealed borer infestations may require whole-structure fumigation or targeted local treatments where registered. Fumigation is carried out only by registered fumigators following fumigation procedures.

European house borer

Where European house borer is suspected, particularly in the Western Cape, follow the official reporting and treatment requirements that apply.

lessons.title: Decay fungi, records and certification
lessons.html:
Treating decay

  1. Find and fix the moisture source: roof leaks, plumbing leaks, rising damp, blocked gutters, poor sub-floor ventilation.
  2. Remove decayed timber, cutting back into sound wood as your procedure or the builder specifies.
  3. Treat remaining adjacent timber with a registered wood preservative where appropriate.
  4. Replace with timber preservative-treated to the correct hazard class.
  5. Improve ventilation and recheck moisture with a meter.

After treatment

  • Clean up dust and debris; remove plugs and drill dust from floors.
  • Clean equipment and dispose of containers correctly.
  • Inform the client of re-entry times and any precautions.

Records

Record the site, organism, extent, treatment method, product and registration number, quantity, areas treated, date, operator and registration. Mark treated areas on a sketch plan.

Certificates and follow-up

Issue a treatment certificate describing the work done. Schedule follow-up inspections, particularly for termites and baiting systems. Where a clearance certificate is needed for property transfer, issue it only when a genuine inspection confirms no active infestation in the accessible timbers. Explain any guarantee and its conditions clearly.

Key points

  • Locate services, water sources and drains before drilling or soil treatment.
  • Use trenching, rodding, drilling and injection or baiting systems for subterranean termites.
  • Clean timber before applying borer treatments and work safely in roof spaces.
  • For decay, fix the moisture source first, then remove and replace timber.
  • Record and certify treatments honestly and schedule follow-ups.
